subject.title: [persistence] thinkingSignature truncated at persist time (literal U+2026 in stored base64) → deterministic 'Invalid signature in thinking block' 400 once prompt cache expires

question: Should Anthropic signature hardening combine source-level persistence integrity, completed-turn replay omission, and repair of existing transcripts, or should the open replay-policy pull request be treated as the complete supported fix?
rationale: These approaches have different durable-data and provider-continuity consequences: replay omission prevents provider rejection, while persistence validation and Doctor repair establish what OpenClaw considers a valid durable transcript and how malformed historical records are rewritten.

options.title: Layered integrity and recovery
options.body: Prevent mutation of opaque signatures, validate before replay, repair existing poisoned records, and land the completed-turn omission only where Anthropic's contract permits it.

options.title: Replay policy only
options.body: Land the completed-turn omission and close the persistence investigation only after proving v2026.7.1 or current main no longer writes new U+2026 signatures.

options.title: Persistence fix only
options.body: Isolate and fix the ellipsis-producing writer while retaining current historical-thinking replay behavior and one-shot recovery.

recommendation.title: Layered integrity and recovery
recommendation.body: Prevent mutation of opaque signatures, validate before replay, repair existing poisoned records, and land the completed-turn omission only where Anthropic's contract permits it.

likelyOwner.reason: They reviewed both the shipped recovery and the open replay-policy implementation, giving them the strongest observed cross-boundary context.
